chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The fasting one and the one in Ihraam do not immerse their head in the water.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: the one in the state of Ihraam (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)
key_terms.يَرْتَمِسُ: to immerse or dip (specifically the head)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on immersing the head in water for a fasting person or one in Ihraam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that a fasting person or one in Ihraam should not fully submerge their head in water, a ruling derived from the principle of preserving the integrity of the worship state and avoiding unnecessary exposure to elements that might invalidate it. This narration highlights the meticulous attention to ritual detail in Shia fiqh, distinguishing between general purification and the specific constraints applied during fasting and pilgrimage.
